findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (and test) that drives `rich_reemit` to 2 on a non-idempotent body and asserts the single post-push GET + `merge_baseline` overlay lands the baseline and converges the loop.
evidence: Context: 'At rich_reemit == 2 do ONE post-push GET for that field and hand the result to _advance_baselines ... as a synced_fields overlay via binding_store.merge_baseline'

Absence: no AC drives rich_reemit to 2 or asserts the merge_baseline overlay resolves the non-idempotent tail
findings.finding: The persisted `rich_reemit` counter and its re-GET-at-==2 convergence path (described at length in Context: incremented on unchanged-sha emit, reset on sha/baseline change, triggering ONE post-push GET handed to `_advance_baselines` via `merge_baseline`) has no covering acceptance criterion that exercises the re-GET path. The only related AC, `test_recanonicalization_converges`, explicitly asserts convergence 'in one re-emit, no re-GET' — i.e. it proves the path BELOW the threshold, never the rich_reemit==2 re-GET/merge_baseline mechanism that the whole counter exists to serve.
scenarios: A body in the non-idempotent tail keeps re-emitting; the ==2 re-GET/merge_baseline logic ships unproven and could loop forever or write the baseline wrong
findings.suggested_fix: Add `test_nonidempotent_tail_reGETs_and_converges` to the AC list: a body whose round-trip is non-idempotent re-emits twice, then at rich_reemit==2 issues exactly one field GET, merges via merge_baseline, and emits zero updates thereafter.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the rich_reemit==2 post-push GET stays conflict-safe: gate the overlay so a remote value that differs from what rebar pushed (i.e. a concurrent peer edit) does NOT seed the baseline, or feed it through the same both-sides conflict check, so a peer edit in the push→GET window still raises outbound-field-conflict rather than being silently clobbered.
evidence: Plan: 'At rich_reemit == 2 do ONE post-push GET for that field and hand the result to _advance_baselines ... as a synced_fields overlay via binding_store.merge_baseline'

merge_baseline contract (peer_state.py:99-104): 'The caller MUST pass only fields whose write is CONFIRMED landed (per-mutation success ...)'; a post-push GET reflects whatever is on the server, not necessarily rebar's write

Conflict detection depends on baseline (outbound_field_diff.py:450-457): fires only when not _local_matches_baseline AND not _remote_matches_baseline; overlaying a peer's value into the baseline makes _remote_matches_baseline True (483-494)
Plan design decision #2 claims conflict safety 'unchanged (a713 local-wins)'
findings.finding: The rich_reemit==2 post-push GET overlays the actual remote value into the baseline via merge_baseline, but cannot distinguish rebar's own landed write from a peer edit that landed between rebar's push and the GET; a concurrent peer edit in that window seeds the baseline with the peer value, causing _remote_matches_baseline to return True and SUPPRESS the both-sides conflict alert on the next pass while local-wins silently clobbers the peer edit.
findings.location: Context/Problem (post-push GET at rich_reemit==2 -> merge_baseline) and Design decisions #2
scenarios: A peer edits the description on the DC/Cloud side after rebar's push but before rebar's post-push GET on the re-emit-2 pass; the peer's edit is written into rebar's baseline as if it were rebar's own synced value
Next pass: rebar re-pushes local (local != baseline), clobbering the peer edit, and no outbound-field-conflict alert is raised
